semantic_candidates.evidence: A regular ring torus with major radius 20 and minor radius 5 millimetres is retained for v in [-pi/3, pi/3] and U span 3*pi/2, then closed by four planes.

validation_findings.evidence: Major radius 20 exceeds minor radius 5 and both retained angular spans are positive, so all four circular arcs and five closure lines have positive length.
Two constant-v major-direction circles, two constant-u minor circles, and five exact lines account for every unique edge.
Both retained parameter intervals are shorter than their full periods, so neither pair of opposite patch boundaries is identified as a seam.
The strict inequality 20>5 defines a regular ring torus rather than horn or spindle geometry, and the parameterisation has no collapsed boundary.
The no-processing STEP round trip records 1e-7 millimetres, equal to 1e-10 metres, for every vertex, edge, and face tolerance.
The toroidal patch, two horizontal v-trim caps, and two radial U closures pair all nine unique boundary edges.
Every edge has exactly two face uses in one connected regular closed component.
V-E+F equals 6-9+5=2 and neither partial periodic interval collapses a boundary.

oracle.statement: The partial U and V intervals define one regular toroidal patch because major radius 20 exceeds minor radius 5. Two major-direction arcs, two minor-direction arcs, four cap-to-radial lines, and one shared axis line give nine edges and six vertices. Two horizontal and two radial planes complete five faces, with every edge used twice.
